description: Third held-out accuracy measurement of 750 public commits (November 2026): lifecycle guards, catalogue and instance ratings, map lookups by an unknown key, and unknown templates

cases.name: a resource whose block had prevent_destroy at the base and is removed is reviewed, naming the guard (source case: Data-Platform 49acecf1f)
a Glue catalog database removed with its prevent_destroy guard is reviewed: its table definitions go with it (source case: Data-Platform 49acecf1f)
a Glue catalog database removed without a guard is still reviewed
a stateful resource removed with its prevent_destroy guard follows the stateful rules and says the guard was there
an EC2 instance replaced by a key_name change is reviewed: its root volume and identity are lost (source case: govwifi-terraform f3289170e)
an EC2 instance whose root volume grows is a possible replacement the provider decides, not reviewed for it
a map looked up by a variable without a default: an edit to another attribute of the map changes nothing read through the lookup (source case: iv-cbv-payroll)
a map looked up by a variable without a default: an attribute read through the lookup whose value changes for one key keeps the possible replacement and names that key
a database engine version change is reviewed: it cannot be rolled back and restarts the database (source case: iv-cbv-payroll 5d02e3b9d)
a launch template whose user_data reads a value from a YAML file that changed is not a proven no-op (source case: terraform-aws-sponsorship 3ad7d9034)
a template file that changed, rendered with variables not known statically, is not a proven no-op
a value that fails to evaluate at both commits, whose expression changed, is not a proven no-op
a value that fails to evaluate at both commits with the same expression is no change
a YAML file whose other values change leaves a value read from it unchanged

base.r/data.yaml:
queues:
  jobs:
    delay: 5
  mail:
    delay: 0
owner: team-a

head.r/data.yaml:
queues:
  jobs:
    delay: 5
  mail:
    delay: 10
owner: team-b

cases.name: a YAML document with a custom tag is not decoded, and a change to it is not a proven no-op
review round 1 (held-out 3): YAML with a merge key is left unknown, so an equivalent rewrite is no proven deletion
review round 1 (held-out 3): a recursive YAML alias is left unknown without crashing
review round 1 (held-out 3): an unquoted YAML date is left unknown, since Terraform rewrites it as a timestamp
review round 1 (held-out 3): reordering the keys of a map read by an unknown key changes nothing
review round 1 (held-out 3): a listener removed with its prevent_destroy guard keeps its traffic rating and names the guard
review round 2 (held-out 3): a YAML scalar Terraform reads as a boolean (yes) is left unknown, so true to yes is no deletion
